questions.question: Name the employee of the English East India Company, who was an engineer and antiquarian who prepared the first survey map of the site of Hampi in 1800.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Colonel Colin Mackenzie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Colonel Colin Mackenzie was the first Surveyor General of India, a position he held from 1815 until his death in 1821.
 
• He is renowned for preparing the first detailed survey map of the site of Hampi in 1800, which was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• Mackenzie was an engineer, surveyor, and antiquarian who had a deep interest in Indian history, culture, and architecture.
 
• He collected manuscripts, inscriptions, and artifacts during his travels, contributing significantly to the study of Indian antiquities and cultural heritage.
 
• His documentation of South Indian history, including the Vijayanagara Empire, serves as a valuable resource for historians and archaeologists today.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Keith Pratt:**

 
 
• Keith Pratt is a scholar known for his contributions to the study of East Asian history and culture, specifically focusing on Korea.
 
• He has no connection to the English East India Company or the survey of Hampi.
 
 
 
• **Sir John Marshall:**
 
 
• Sir John Marshall was a British archaeologist and the Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) from 1902 to 1928.
 
• He is best known for his work in excavating the sites of the Indus Valley Civilization, such as Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro.
 
• His contributions are significant in the field of Indian archaeology, but he was not involved in the survey of Hampi.
 
 
 
• **William Lambton:**
 
 
• William Lambton was a British geographer and surveyor who initiated the Great Trigonometrical Survey of India in 1802.
 
• This survey aimed to map the Indian subcontinent and measure the curvature of the Earth.
 
• Although a prominent figure in surveying, his work was unrelated to the historical site of Hampi.

questions.question: Which Act first recognised the political and administrative functions of the East India Company in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regulating Act 1773**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** was the first parliamentary legislation by the British government to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.
 
• This Act marked the **beginning of British political and administrative control** in India.
 
• It established the position of the **Governor-General of Bengal** (later known as Governor-General of India) and created an executive council to assist him.
 
• The Act aimed to address the **administrative corruption** and financial mismanagement by the East India Company.
 
• The **Supreme Court of Judicature at Calcutta** was also established under this Act, marking the start of a structured judicial system in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charter Act of 1813**

 
 
• This Act ended the trade monopoly of the East India Company, except for trade in tea and trade with China.
 
• It allowed missionaries to spread education and Christianity in India.
 
• The Act allocated funds for the promotion of education in India.
 
 
 
• **Pitt's India Act 1784**
 
 
• This Act distinguished between the **commercial and political functions** of the East India Company.
 
• A Board of Control was established to supervise the Company's political affairs in India.
 
• The Governor-General's authority was strengthened by this Act.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act 1858**
 
 
• This Act abolished the East India Company's rule in India and transferred the administration to the British Crown.
 
• The position of the Governor-General of India was replaced by the **Viceroy of India**.
 
• It marked the beginning of direct governance of India by the British Government.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court of Judicature**
 
 
• Established by the Regulating Act of 1773, it was the first British court in India.
 
• Located in Calcutta, the court had jurisdiction over British subjects and Company officials.
 
• It marked the foundation of the modern judicial system in India.

questions.question:
Who among the following were the painters of Shahjahan?

(a) Muhammad Nadir Samarqandi

(b) Adbus Samad

(c) Mir Hshim

(d) Mir Saiyid Ali
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Shah Jahan (1628-58)** was the fifth Mughal emperor of India. He was the third son of the Mughal emperor Jahangir.
 
• During Shah Jahan there was a decrease in figure-color and color-coordination. However, a progress made in drawing and border making.
 
• Shahjahan liked to make his paintings in Divine version. Famous painters of his time – Fakir Ulla**, Mir Hashim**, Murar, Hunar Muhammad Nadir, **Muhammad Nadir Samarqandi** and Chitra were prominent.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mīr Sayyid ʿAli,** (flourished 16th century, India), Persian miniaturist who, together with his fellow countryman **ʿ****Abduṣ-Ṣamad**, emigrated to India and helped to found the Mughal school of painting.
 
• **Adbus Samad** followed Humayun to India in 1548. He instructed both Humāyūn and his young son, the future emperor Akbar, in drawing. 
 
• The two most notable works accomplished by them during the reign of Akbar was Tutinama and Hamza Nama.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Under Shah Jahan, Mughal campaigns continued in the Deccan. The Afghan noble Khan Jahan Lodi rebelled and was defeated. Campaigns were launched against Ahmadnagar; the Bundelas were defeated and Orchha seized.
 
• In 1632 Ahmadnagar was finally annexed and the Bijapur forces sued for peace.
 
• In 1657-1658, there was conflict over succession amongst Shah Jahan’s sons. Aurangzeb was victorious and his three brothers, including Dara Shukoh, were killed.
 
• Shah Jahan was imprisoned for the rest of his life in Agra.
 
• It was during Shah Jahan’s reign that the different elements of Mughal architecture were fused together in a grand harmonious synthesis.
 
• His reign witnessed a huge amount of construction activity especially in Agra and Delhi. The ceremonial halls of public and private audience (diwan-i khas o am) were carefully planned. Shah Jahan’s audience halls were specially constructed to resemble a mosque.
 
• The pedestal on which his throne was placed was frequently described as the qibla, the direction faced by Muslims at prayer, since everybody faced that direction when court was in session.
 
• The idea of the king as a representative of God on earth was suggested by these architectural features.
 
• Shah Jahan adapted the river-front garden in the layout of the Taj Mahal, the grandest architectural accomplishment of his reign.
 
• He develops this architectural form as a means to control the access that nobles had to the river.
 
• In the new city of Shahjahanabad that he constructed in Delhi, the imperial palace commanded the river-front. Only specially favoured nobles – like his eldest son Dara Shukoh – were given access to the river. All others had to construct their homes in the city away from the River Yamuna.

questions.question: In Koppen's climatic classification ET and EF is identified by:

options.text: Soil is permanently frozen to depths of hundreds of meters.
Year-round cold temperatures with the warmest month less than 10 °C.
Vegetation is dominated by mosses, lichens, dwarf trees and scattered woody shrubs.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is:** "All of the given options"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Köppen Climate Classification – ET and EF:**

 
 
• ET (Tundra) and EF (Ice Cap) climates are part of the polar climate group in Köppen's classification.
 
• ET is characterized by tundra vegetation, with mosses, lichens, dwarf trees, and scattered woody shrubs due to short growing seasons and permafrost.
 
• EF climates, or ice cap climates, are extremely cold year-round, with soil permanently frozen to depths of hundreds of meters (permafrost) and minimal or no vegetation.
 
• Both ET and EF climates have cold temperatures throughout the year, with the warmest month usually below 10 °C, preventing tree growth in most areas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soil Permanently Frozen:**

 
 
• EF climates are defined by ice caps where the soil remains frozen year-round, often to depths of hundreds of meters.
 
• This permafrost prevents plant roots from penetrating, limiting vegetation to non-existent or sparse forms.
 
 
 
• **Year-round Cold Temperatures:**
 
 
• Both ET and EF climates experience consistently low temperatures, with the warmest month not exceeding 10 °C.
 
• These low temperatures significantly influence ecosystem characteristics and human settlement patterns.
 
 
 
• **Vegetation Characteristics:**
 
 
• ET climates support tundra vegetation, including mosses, lichens, dwarf trees, and scattered shrubs.
 
• EF climates usually have negligible vegetation due to permanent ice cover and extremely cold conditions.

questions.question: Lala Lajpat Rai, Indian revolutionary politician and author was also recognised by which of the following title?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab Kesari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai** was a prominent leader in the **Indian Independence Movement**. He was known for his dedication to the nation and his ability to inspire people towards achieving freedom.
 
• He was given the title **"Punjab Kesari"**, meaning the **"Lion of Punjab"**, due to his fearless attitude and contributions to the freedom struggle.
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai was one of the **Lal-Bal-Pal trio**, alongside Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal, who were pivotal in promoting the extremist approach in the **Indian Nationalist Movement**.
 
• He played a significant role in the **Swadeshi Movement** and encouraged Indians to boycott British goods and adopt indigenous products. *Hence, the correct answer is Punjab Kesari.*
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai also protested against the **Simon Commission** in 1928, during which he suffered injuries in a police lathi-charge that eventually led to his death.
 
• Titles like **Mahamana (given to Madan Mohan Malaviya)**, **Tilak of Punjab**, and **Deshbandhu (given to Chittaranjan Das)** are unrelated to Lala Lajpat Rai. *Hence, the correct title for Lala Lajpat Rai is Punjab Kesari.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai’s Contributions:**

 
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai** was born on **28 January 1865** in Punjab. He was an ardent nationalist and a social reformer.
 
• He was associated with the **Indian National Congress** and believed in achieving independence through stronger measures, which made him one of the prominent leaders of the **extremist wing**.
 
• He founded the **Punjab National Bank** in 1894, which aimed to promote indigenous banking and economic independence.
 
 
 
• **Titles and Recognitions:**
 
 
• The title **"Punjab Kesari"** was attributed to him due to his courage and leadership during the freedom struggle.
 
• Other titles like **Mahamana** were associated with **Madan Mohan Malaviya**, and **Deshbandhu** was given to **Chittaranjan Das**.
 
• The title **Tilak of Punjab** is not officially recorded for Lala Lajpat Rai.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai’s sacrifice during the protest against the **Simon Commission** is considered one of the turning points in India's struggle for independence.
 
• His writings, speeches, and leadership continue to inspire generations of Indians.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Simon Commission Protest:**

 
 
• **Simon Commission** was boycotted by Indians as it did not include any Indian members.
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai led the protest in **Lahore** on **30 October 1928**, where he suffered fatal injuries due to the police lathi-charge.
 
 
 
• **Contributions to Literature:**
 
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai authored several books, including **"Unhappy India"**, which critiqued British policies.
 
• His works reflected his vision of a free and prosperous India.

questions.question: During which five year plan, the Steel Plants at Bhilai, Rourkela, and Durgapur were built?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Second Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961)** in India focused on the rapid industrialization of the country with an emphasis on heavy industries.
 
• During this plan, three major integrated steel plants were established at **Bhilai (Madhya Pradesh, now Chhattisgarh), Rourkela (Odisha), and Durgapur (West Bengal)**.
 
• The establishment of these steel plants was a part of the plan to build a strong industrial base for India’s economic development.
 
• The **Bhilai Steel Plant** was set up with assistance from the Soviet Union, **Rourkela Steel Plant** with German collaboration, and the **Durgapur Steel Plant** with British collaboration.
 
• The Second Plan was based on the **Mahalanobis Model**, which emphasized the development of heavy industries as a strategy for long-term economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Plan (1951-1956):**
 
 
• The First Five Year Plan focused on the development of the primary sector, particularly **agriculture, irrigation, and power generation**.
 
• It aimed to address the challenges of food shortages and inflation after independence.
 
• The primary projects during this period included **multipurpose river valley projects** like the Bhakra-Nangal Dam and Hirakud Dam.
 
• Its success laid the foundation for subsequent economic planning in India.
 
 
 
• **Third Plan (1961-1966):**
 
 
• The Third Five Year Plan shifted focus to **self-reliance in production and economic stability**.
 
• It emphasized agriculture to meet the food requirements of the growing population and the development of industries to reduce dependence on imports.
 
• However, the plan was disrupted due to the **Sino-Indian War of 1962**, Indo-Pak War of 1965, and severe droughts.
 
 
 
• **Plan Holiday (1966-1969):**
 
 
• The period between 1966 and 1969 is referred to as the **Plan Holiday** due to economic instability caused by wars and droughts.
 
• Rather than long-term plans, the government focused on **annual plans** to stabilize the economy.
 
• Key emphasis was placed on addressing the food crisis, improving agricultural productivity, and controlling inflation.

questions.question: Which of the following constitutional mechanisms ensures political representation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Indian Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 330 and 332**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 330** of the Indian Constitution provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the Lok Sabha.
 
• **Article 332** ensures the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Legislative Assemblies of the states.
 
• The representation for SCs and STs is designed to ensure their political participation and address historical social inequalities.
 
• These provisions are part of India's constitutional safeguards to promote inclusivity and equality in governance.
 
• The reservation is based on the proportion of population of SCs and STs in each state or union territory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 15 and 16:** These articles prohibit discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth and ensure equality in public employment, but they do not directly deal with reservation in Parliament.
 
• **Article 341 and 342:** These articles define Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, providing the framework for their identification but do not outline political representation mechanisms.
 
• **Article 338 and 339:** These articles establish special commissions for the welfare of SCs and STs and directives for their development, focusing on their socio-economic progress rather than direct political representation.
 
• The reservation of seats in Parliament and state legislatures for SCs and STs is reviewed periodically, and provisions are extended by constitutional amendments as required.
 
• India's democracy ensures that marginalized communities have a voice in governance by providing these constitutional safeguards.

questions.question: Which of the following territories was annexed by the British Governor General Lord Dalhousie before the 1857 revolt that fueled the First War of Independence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Awadh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord Dalhousie annexed **Awadh** in 1856, under the pretext of misgovernance and maladministration.
 
• The annexation was carried out under the controversial **Doctrine of Lapse**, although the official reason cited was maladministration.
 
• The annexation of Awadh caused widespread resentment among the local population, particularly the sepoys, who were recruited heavily from this region.
 
• The discontent in Awadh became one of the primary reasons for the widespread participation of the region in the **1857 Revolt**.
 
• The people of Awadh, especially the dispossessed landlords and the sepoys, played a significant role in the rebellion, making the annexation a key trigger for the First War of Independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Doctrine of Lapse:**

 
 
• Introduced by Lord Dalhousie, it allowed the British to annex Indian states where the ruler died without a legitimate male heir.
 
• This policy was widely criticized and became a major cause of unrest among Indian princely states.
 
 
 
• **Reasons for the 1857 Revolt:**
 
 
• Annexation of territories like Awadh, Satara, and Jhansi under the Doctrine of Lapse.
 
• Economic exploitation, social reforms perceived as interference, and military grievances among sepoys.
 
 
 
• **Role of Awadh in 1857:**
 
 
• Awadh became a center of rebellion, with its dispossessed landlords and sepoys actively participating.
 
• Leaders like Begum Hazrat Mahal emerged as prominent figures in the revolt from Awadh.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Awadh’s Annexation:**
 
 
• It exposed the exploitative nature of British policies, leading to a loss of trust among Indian rulers and subjects.
 
• The annexation directly affected the lives of thousands, fueling widespread anger against the British administration.

questions.question: India formally adopted inflation targeting under a Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option 2 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• In March 2025, RBI reaffirmed that inflation targeting remains its primary objective, even as food inflation pushed CPI above 6%, breaching the upper tolerance band.
 
• The Government of India (March 2021 notification) had extended the FIT framework till 2026, confirming the 4% ±2% band.
 
• Debate continues on whether RBI should shift to a dual mandate (growth + inflation), especially after pandemic shocks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• India did not adopt inflation targeting during the 1991 reforms. Policy was focused on structural liberalisation, fiscal consolidation, and exchange rate reforms. **Hence, Option A is incorrect. **
 
• After the East Asian crisis, India adopted prudential banking and capital account management, but not formal inflation targeting. **Hence, Option B is incorrect. **
 
• India adopted Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) through an amendment to the RBI Act, 1934, giving statutory basis to the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC). The inflation target was set at 4% with a tolerance band of ±2%. **Hence, Option C is correct. **
 
• In 2020, the focus was on liquidity infusion under Atmanirbhar Bharat, not adoption of FIT. **Hence, Option D is incorrect. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Statutory Basis: Section 45ZB of RBI Act empowers the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).
 
• MPC Composition: 6 members (3 RBI + 3 Govt nominees), chaired by RBI Governor.
 
• Why “Flexible”? Unlike strict inflation targeting, FIT allows consideration of growth and financial stability.
 
• Measure Used: CPI (Combined) is the nominal anchor for inflation targeting.
 
• Global Context:
 
 
• New Zealand (1990) was the first to adopt inflation targeting.
 
• UK, Canada, South Africa, and Brazil follow similar frameworks.
 
 
 
• India’s Inflation History:
 
 
• Pre-2016: WPI was the main inflation measure.
 
• Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended CPI-based inflation targeting.
 
 
 
• Advantages of FIT: Predictability, macroeconomic stability, anchor for expectations.
 
• Criticism: In developing economies like India, inflation is often driven by supply shocks (food, fuel), limiting effectiveness of monetary tightening.

questions.question: In plant cells, the cytoplasmic channels allowing communication and transport between adjacent cells are formed by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plasmodesmata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Plasmodesmata** are microscopic cytoplasmic channels that connect adjacent plant cells, facilitating communication and the transport of substances.
 
• They allow the exchange of molecules like nutrients, ions, and signaling compounds, ensuring coordination between plant cells.
 
• Plasmodesmata are formed during cell division, remaining as connections between the daughter cells.
 
• Their structure includes a narrow tube-like extension of the endoplasmic reticulum, called the desmotubule, surrounded by cytoplasmic sleeves.
 
• These channels are essential for maintaining plant tissue integrity and coordinating developmental and physiological processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adherens Junctions**

 
 
• These are cell-cell junctions found in animal cells that connect the actin cytoskeleton of adjacent cells.
 
• They help maintain the structural integrity of tissues and play a role in cell signaling and tissue morphogenesis.
 
• Adherens junctions are composed of cadherin proteins that link to actin filaments via catenins.
 
 
 
• **Hemidesmosomes**
 
 
• These are specialized junctions found in animal cells that anchor epithelial cells to the basement membrane.
 
• They contain integrin proteins that connect the intermediate filaments of cells to extracellular matrix components like laminin.
 
• Hemidesmosomes provide mechanical stability to tissues, especially under stress.
 
 
 
• **Septate Junctions**
 
 
• These are cell-cell junctions found in invertebrates, functioning similarly to tight junctions in vertebrates.
 
• They form a barrier to regulate the movement of molecules between cells, maintaining tissue compartmentalization.
 
• Septate junctions are commonly found in epithelial tissues of insects and other arthropods.

questions.question: Chlorine works best as a disinfectant when the pH of water is around _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7**__.

__
 
• Chlorination is a chemical disinfection method that uses various types of chlorine or chlorine-containing substances for the oxidation and disinfection of what will be the potable water source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Chlorine, **whether **in the form of pure chlorine **gas **from a cylinder, **sodium hypochlorite**, or **calcium hypochlorite** in any of its presentations, **dissolves in water to form hypochlorous and hydrochloric acids**.
 
• A **pH between 6.5 and 8.5** will see both hypochlorous acid and hypochlorite ions present in the water.
 
• Together, the hypochlorous acid and the hypochlorite ions are referred to as free chlorine.
 
• Hypochlorous acid is the more effective disinfectant, and therefore, a **lower pH is preferred for disinfection**.
 
• **Calcium hypochlorite** (CaOCl) is made up of the calcium salts of hypochlorous acid. It is produced by dissolving chlorine gas (Cl₂) into a solution of calcium oxide (CaO) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH).
 
• **Sodium hypochlorite** (NaOCl) is made up of the sodium salts of hypochlorous acid and is a chlorine-containing compound that can be used as a disinfectant. It is produced when chlorine gas is dissolved into a sodium hydroxide solution.
 
• The reaction of chlorine in water follows the reaction shown below:
 
 
• **Cl₂ + H₂0 →HOCl + HCl**
 
• Hydrochloric acid dissociates in turn to form hydrogen and chloride ions HCl → H⁺ + Cl⁻
 
• Hypochlorous acid however dissociates only partially HOCl ⇔ H⁺ + OCl⁻

questions.question: Tarun Bhattacharya, who was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018, is known for playing which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Santoor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• **Santoor**

 
 
• The Santoor is a hammered dulcimer, a stringed musical instrument originating from the valleys of Kashmir in India.
 
• It consists of a wooden trapezoid-shaped body with numerous strings stretched across it, played by striking the strings with a pair of curved mallets.
 
• The Santoor is commonly used in Indian classical music and is known for its distinct, melodious sound.
 
• The instrument has a significant presence in Sufi music and has been incorporated into various musical genres over time.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**
 
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is a national honor bestowed by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy of Music, Dance & Drama.
 
• It was established in 1952 to recognize and reward outstanding achievements in the performing arts.
 
• Recipients of the award are given a citation, a cash prize, and a shawl as a mark of honor.
 
• This prestigious award is a testament to an artist's dedication and excellence in their respective field.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Music**
 
 
• Indian classical music is a rich tradition that dates back thousands of years and is categorized into two major traditions: Hindustani (North Indian) and Carnatic (South Indian).
 
• It is characterized by intricate ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic cycles) that form the basis of compositions and improvisations.
 
• Instruments like the sitar, tabla, veena, and santoor play pivotal roles in Indian classical music performances.
 
• The music is deeply spiritual, often associated with various deities and used in religious and ceremonial contexts.

questions.question: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution distributes legislative powers between the Union and State governments, listing Union, State, and Concurrent List subjects?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seventh Schedule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Indian Constitution specifies the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and State governments.
 
• It comprises three distinct lists: **Union List, State List, and Concurrent List**, which categorize subjects under the jurisdiction of the Union, State, or both.
 
• The **Union List** contains subjects such as defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways, which are exclusively legislated by the Parliament.
 
• The **State List** includes subjects such as police, public health, agriculture, and local government, which fall under the purview of State Legislatures.
 
• The **Concurrent List** encompasses subjects like education, marriage, and adoption, where both the Union and State governments can legislate. However, in case of a conflict, Union law prevails.
 
• The distribution of powers in the Seventh Schedule ensures smooth governance and maintains the federal structure of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Third Schedule:**
 
 
• The Third Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains forms of oaths and affirmations for various constitutional posts, including the President, Vice-President, Ministers, Members of Parliament, and Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts.
 
• It ensures accountability and adherence to constitutional provisions by individuals holding public offices.
 
 
 
• **Ninth Schedule:**
 
 
• The Ninth Schedule was added to the Constitution through the First Amendment in 1951 to protect certain laws from judicial review.
 
• It contains laws related to land reforms and abolition of the zamindari system, aimed at promoting social and economic equality.
 
• However, the Supreme Court ruled in the **Keshavananda Bharati case (1973)** that laws in the Ninth Schedule could still be challenged if they violate the basic structure of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Eleventh Schedule:**
 
 
• The Eleventh Schedule was introduced by the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, which deals with the Panchayati Raj system.
 
• It lists 29 subjects over which Panchayats are granted authority to prepare plans and implement schemes for economic development and social justice.
 
• Subjects include agriculture, rural housing, health, sanitation, and education, among others.

questions.question: When was the Prime Minister Jan Dhan Yojana announced?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fri Aug 15 2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)** was announced by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** in his Independence Day speech on **15th August 2014**.
 
• The scheme was formally launched on **28th August 2014** with the aim of achieving **financial inclusion** by providing universal access to banking facilities.
 
• The scheme's primary objective was to ensure that every household in the country has access to at least one bank account, with a focus on **poor and underprivileged sections**.
 
• It offers basic banking services such as **saving accounts**, access to **credit**, **insurance**, and **pension** facilities.
 
• The scheme also provides a **RuPay Debit Card** with an in-built accident insurance cover of **Rs. 1 lakh**, later extended to **Rs. 2 lakhs** for accounts opened after 28th August 2018.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Objectives of Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana:**
 
 
• To achieve **financial inclusion** by providing affordable access to financial services such as **bank accounts, remittances, credit, insurance, and pensions**.
 
• To enable the direct transfer of subsidies and other government benefits into beneficiary accounts, reducing **leakages** and ensuring transparency.
 
• To promote the habit of **savings** and ensure access to **micro-credit** and **insurance** facilities for the underprivileged.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of PMJDY:**
 
 
• **Zero Balance Accounts:** Beneficiaries can open a basic savings account without the requirement of maintaining a minimum balance.
 
• **Overdraft Facility:** An overdraft facility of up to **Rs. 10,000** is provided for one account per household, preferably held by women.
 
• **Accidental Insurance Cover:** Initially, Rs. 1 lakh accidental insurance coverage was provided, later increased to Rs. 2 lakhs for new accounts.
 
• **Life Insurance:** A life insurance cover of Rs. 30,000 is provided to eligible beneficiaries.
 
 
 
• **Achievements of PMJDY:**
 
 
• As of **October 2023**, over **50 crore accounts** have been opened under the scheme, with a significant proportion belonging to rural and semi-urban areas.
 
• The total balance in PMJDY accounts stands at over **Rs. 2 lakh crore**, demonstrating its impact on financial inclusion.
 
• More than **67% of PMJDY accounts** have been opened by women, empowering them financially.
 
 
 
• **Important Initiatives Linked to PMJDY:**
 
 
• **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT):** Subsidies and other government benefits are directly transferred to PMJDY accounts, reducing middlemen and ensuring transparency.
 
• **RuPay Debit Cards:** These cards facilitate cashless transactions and also provide accidental insurance coverage.
 
• **Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) Trinity:** PMJDY accounts are integrated with Aadhaar and mobile numbers to enable seamless benefit transfers and promote digital banking.
 
 
</ul
